assessmentSummary.identity: From one declared support leg, project forward through flight, land on the opposite leg, absorb to a stable terminal hold for the declared duration without an extra hop or free-foot touch, then reset fully before the next attempt.
currentCardFindings: The legacy name Bound to Stick omits direction and landing-side contract even though its description says one leg to the other and its planning summary says horizontal projection.

Bound convention alone is not enough for deterministic selection because same-leg forward hops, opposite-leg forward bounds, lateral bounds, diagonal bounds, continuous bounds, and reactive bounds have different contacts and loading.
The existing card requires a freeze and reset, so this audit preserves a discrete terminal-stick identity rather than converting it to continuous bounding.
Five exact-title candidates returned current YouTube oEmbed metadata and iframe markup; movement, safety, accessibility, and demonstration approval remain human-review gates.

proposedDosage.progressWhen: both directions of side transfer preserve projection intent quiet whole-foot absorption alignment declared hold and full reset

athleteInstructions: Confirm the forward lane and landing zone are clear, dry, level, and long enough for a safe miss.
Start on the declared takeoff leg with the opposite thigh and arms ready to drive.
Project forward, travel through flight, and land on the opposite leg; do not turn the rep into a same-leg hop.
Absorb through the foot, ankle, knee, and hip with the pelvis and trunk controlled.
Hold for the declared duration without another hop or free-foot touch, then step out and reset fully.

assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Retain the stable bound-to-stick slug but rename and constrain the selectable baseline to an opposite-leg forward bound with terminal hold and full reset. Preserve the generic legacy label as an alias only. Keep the card review-only until content, media, scoring, relationship, pilot, and card reviewers approve it.

claims: World Athletics describes alternate-leg bounding as horizontal and vertical projection from one leg to the other.
This card adds a discrete terminal hold and full reset; forward direction, opposite-leg landing, hold, and reset are identity requirements rather than optional cues.
Forward, diagonal, and lateral jump-landings produce direction-specific postural-stability demands.
Direction and landing side therefore remain controlled taxonomy fields and are not interchangeable aliases.
Forward single-leg landing uses coordinated foot, ankle, knee, hip, pelvis, and trunk absorption.
The opposite-leg takeoff-to-landing transition also requires contralateral swing and single-leg stabilization.
Landing direction changes whole-body configuration and joint energy-absorption strategy.
No exact force, distance, or transfer claim is inferred for this coaching card.
Single-leg bounding is a high-intensity plyometric relative to double-leg hopping.
Overall exercise difficulty is the maximum of exercise complexity and physical difficulty; athlete proficiency is excluded.
Plyometrics rapidly accelerate and decelerate body mass and should not be performed while fatigued.
Every landing contact counts toward impact and overlapping sprint, jump, Achilles, knee, hip, and lower-body budgets.
Plyometric guidance calls for shock-absorbing surfaces, adequate space, warm-up, progression, and proper technique.
The forward lane and landing zone are hard selection constraints.
Plyometric volume is tracked by contacts and power work needs long recovery.
The proposed attempts, caps, and rest are conservative coaching proposals requiring pilot calibration.
A reproducible jump-landing task must declare direction and stabilization finish.
Instructions separately state takeoff leg, forward direction, opposite landing leg, absorption, hold, and reset.
Single-leg landing force and time to stabilization are meaningful task outcomes.
Stop rules use observable contact, alignment, stabilization, symptoms, and output changes without claiming injury prediction.
High-quality plyometrics should be placed before fatiguing work and given sufficient recovery.
Use this card for discrete forward power and braking, not conditioning or continuous bounding.
Athletes need a visible finish standard and a clear distinction between effort and symptoms.
Support content must show the exact opposite-leg landing, hold, reset, expected effort, and stop path in text as well as video.
Direction-specific landing mechanics should not be inferred from a generic bound label.
Record takeoff side, landing side, direction, distance, hold, contacts, rest, surface, quality, symptoms, and stop reason.
Lower-intensity progression should precede complex plyometric exposure.
Scale distance, intent, contacts, target width, hold, and rest while preserving forward direction and opposite-leg landing.
Forward, diagonal, and lateral tasks have distinct stabilization demands.
Same-leg landing, continuous cadence, diagonal direction, lateral direction, approach, external load, or reactive response require an explicit variant or separate definition.
